therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Adults with symptomatic restless legs syndrome (RLS) associated with chronic kidney disease (CKD) managed with haemodialysis
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Change in IRLS Rating Scale Total Score at Week 12

results.effect_size: IRLS mean score at Week 12: ropinirole IR 15.9 vs placebo 9.2 (completers only; n=12 vs 5)
subgroup_findings: At Week 12 (completers), IRLS mean score was 15.9 (ropinirole IR, n=12) vs 9.2 (placebo, n=5)
At Week 12 (completers), PSQI total score was 7.3 (ropinirole IR) vs 8.6 (placebo)
At Week 12 (completers), RLSQOL overall life impact score was 85.63 (ropinirole IR) vs 90.50 (placebo)
CGI-I at Week 12: 5/12 ropinirole IR participants rated 'very much' or 'much improved' vs 4/5 placebo participants
17 participants were prematurely withdrawn before Week 12
safety_signals: Acute coronary syndrome reported in 1/22 ropinirole IR participants (serious)
Atrial flutter reported in 1/12 placebo participants (serious)
Upper respiratory tract infection reported in 1/12 placebo participants (serious)

dose_info.schedule: once daily within 1–3 hours before bedtime; titrated in increments of 0.5 mg/day
dose_info.dose_modifications: Dose upward titrated from 0.25 mg/day to 0.5 mg/day then in increments of 0.5 mg/day up to 3 mg/day targeting CGI-I 'much improved' or 'very much improved'

context.indication: Restless legs syndrome associated with chronic kidney disease managed with haemodialysis
context.duration: 12-week double-blind period; up to 64-week long-term open-label period
context.investigator_commentary: Trial was terminated because GSK concluded that it was impossible to recruit sufficient participants within a reasonable timeframe.
